product_family: Task management and collaboration platform with personal, family, and team tiers. Includes task lists, calendar integration, AI assistant (does not train on customer data), integrations with 6000+ apps, and team collaboration features.

certifications.name: SOC 2 (Type 1 or Type 2)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of SOC 2 certification in Any.do's published documentation.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. No ISO 27001 certification mentioned in privacy policy, help center, or public documentation.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Not mentioned in any accessible vendor documentation.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Not mentioned in vendor documentation.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of FedRAMP authorization.

certifications.name: GDPR Compliance Posture
certifications.proof_quote: Privacy policy states: 'access from Israel is covered by the Adequacy Decision issued by the European Commission about Israel.' GDPR data processing practices documented in privacy policy.

privacy.ai_training_note: Any.do explicitly states in their privacy policy: 'we do not use or retain data obtained through these APIs to train, improve, or develop non-personalized machine learning (ML) or artificial intelligence (AI) models.' The platform includes an AI assistant feature that does not train on customer data.
privacy.data_region: Not publicly specified. Company headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel. No data residency options mentioned.

security.name: Encryption in Transit
security.value: Yes, stated as 'Data is encrypted in transit when syncing between devices and Any.do servers.' Specific standard (TLS version) not specified.

security.name: Encryption at Rest
security.value: Not explicitly documented. Privacy policy mentions 'appropriate technical, organizational and security measures' but does not specify encryption at rest details.

security.name: Two-Factor Authentication
security.value: Available. Security code sent to email on new device session.

products.name: Any.do Personal
products.data_scope: Personal tasks, lists, reminders, calendar integration
products.notes: Free tier available. Freemium model. No special security considerations vs team tier.

products.name: Any.do Family
products.data_scope: Shared family boards, grocery lists, household projects, family member tasks
products.notes: Shared but private to family members. Same underlying infrastructure as personal tier.

products.name: Any.do Team/Workspace
products.data_scope: Team projects, boards, task assignments, shared calendars, integrations with 6000+ apps
products.notes: Paid tier. No mention of enterprise-grade security features or SLA-based support. Same compliance posture as personal tier.

compare.pricing_model: Freemium with paid premium tiers. No per-seat pricing detailed in public docs.
compare.data_residency: Not customizable. Single global deployment from Israel.

flags: No enterprise-grade certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001) despite 40M+ user base. Suggests product positioned for consumers/SMBs, not enterprise.
Company has ~15 employees managing 40M+ users, indicating lean infrastructure team. Raises questions about security operations maturity.
Encryption at rest not explicitly documented. Privacy policy only mentions 'appropriate measures' without specifics.
No Data Processing Agreement (DPA) mentioned or linked in privacy policy. May hinder B2B enterprise sales requiring DPA.

Privacy policy includes broad liability disclaimers: 'we cannot guarantee that the information will not be exposed as a result of unauthorized penetration to our servers.' This is a notable caveat on data protection promises.
No dedicated trust center or security documentation page. Security information scattered across help articles and legal docs.
Data center locations and infrastructure providers not publicly disclosed.
No vulnerability disclosure program or bug bounty program mentioned.
Headquartered in Israel (outside EU/US data hub). May trigger data residency concerns for some enterprise customers despite adequacy decision.
